blocks.text: Penicillins are a group of bactericidal antibiotics derived from Penicillium fungi. They treat many bacterial infections by inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis and are highly effective against Gram-positive bacteria, including streptococcal and staphylococcal infections. Penicillin was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain and skin rashes.

items: It targets bacteria, because animal cells lack the cell walls the drug acts on.
It interrupts the cross-linking of peptidoglycan (murein) chains, stopping new cell wall synthesis.
The weakened wall can no longer hold the cell together and it bursts (lysis), so penicillin kills bacteria rather than just stopping their growth.
Some bacteria resist it by producing enzymes such as beta-lactamases.
